item.title: Ebola tops 11,000 cases in Congo's deadliest outbreak
item.description: Congo's Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, the government said Wednesday, a stark figure that underscores the severity of the situation as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease.
item.content:encoded:

(Image credit: Sebastien Kitsa Musayi)

item.title: Seven days of chaos in the ER: How this country's healthcare system is unraveling
item.description: Renewed fighting has pushed Ethiopia's healthcare system close to collapse: "The whole emergency (room) was flooded with war trauma patients," one surgeon says of a brutal week in September.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Why honesty is not always the best policy
item.description: Should you tell your boss she's got food on her face? Your partner you hate their outfit? Social psychologist Vanessa Bohns shares advice on when to tell someone the truth — or keep your mouth shut.

item.title: How word of mouth is helping an Amish community's fight against measles
item.description: In Pennsylvania, health officials use a quiet vaccination campaign designed to win the trust of the state's Amish community, which has been hit hard by the measles outbreak.

item.title: How Medicaid affected one California House race
item.description: A Republican in California's Central Valley fended off challengers for years. But his district had a lot of people on Medicaid, and he lost by a large margin this time.

item.title: One air ambulance service rethinks what it takes to practice medicine in the sky
item.description: Air medical service comes with high risks, high costs, and staffing struggles. To reduce turnover and serve rural patients, LifeFlight of Maine is putting the needs of healthcare workers first.

item.title: A promising new medicine against heart disease fails unexpectedly
item.description: Doctors expected an experimental drug that lowers a common risk factor for heart attacks would save patients' lives. The medicine made no difference.
